RT-6 by the letter of 9.1 c13 scans app/server/http/*.js, and http/body.js holds readText with `new HttpError("bad_encoding")`, a code outside AUTH_CODES; no file of server/ or api/ imports readText (dead code), so no route answers it. RT-6 leaves out the codes inside readText only while no file imports readText (checked in the test; a planted importer makes bad_encoding count). Alternative for CODE-DESIGNER/CODE-FIXER: drop the unused readText.

RT-6 reads two forms more than 9.1 names: `refusal("…")` (the returned refusals of routes/auth.js and admin.js pass their code through refusal()) and `errorBody("…")` (app.js); without them the returned codes (invalid_credentials, reset_invalid, totp_invalid, not_found) would be outside the scan.

Mutants not killable by this lane's int tests: M7 (setup by a select first) — PGlite serialises transactions (F9), so SU-3 cannot see it; AUTH-RACE-5 (two parallel setups on Postgres) is added to the pg file for it. M52 (the admin's login_delays row read without for update) — on Postgres too, step 7 of the pipeline upserts the rate_limits row of the same address (same addressKey) and holds its row lock to the end of the transaction, so parallel attempts from one address are serialised before they reach login_delays: AUTH-RACE-3 holds as a behaviour test but cannot tell M52 from the code (an equivalent mutant while the login limit is counted per address). M37 (no transaction deadline) — ADD-1 still answers within 5 s because the pg adapter's own query_timeout (3000 ms) ends a silent statement; the guard itself is killed by ADD-2 (M37b). M19, M22 not applied.
